title: Letter and Will
premise: Elodie Sandoval, the meticulous concierge of the Hotel Verlaine in the small town of Ashcombe, is paid an enormous advance by a nervous stranger named Corin Vale to prove that a murder has not yet happened. Following his cryptic instructions, she uncovers a ledger disguised as the hotel's decades-old guest registry — a coded record of debts, favors, and one scheduled killing tied to the town's founding families. As Elodie deciphers it, she realizes the intended victim is Corin himself, and that her own late father's name appears among the ledger's keepers. In the end, Elodie must choose between exposing the conspiracy through legal channels, which would destroy the town and implicate her father, or enforcing the ledger's own brutal code of restitution outside the law — a choice she resolves by turning the ledger against its keepers, forcing public confession on the eve of the murder date.
about_author: Theo Thornbury is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who spent eleven years in grand hotels across New England, collecting the small confessions guests make at 3 a.m. He writes mysteries about people who see everything and are seen by no one.

chapters.title: The Advance
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. A gaunt stranger, Corin Vale, checks into the Hotel Verlaine and pays a year's lodging upfront with one condition: Elodie must prove, within thirty days, that a murder has not yet occurred. He refuses to say whose. The chapter establishes Elodie's gift for noticing — the wrong cufflinks, a rehearsed limp — and ends with her uneasy acceptance. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Searching her mental files of guest habits for anything 'murder-shaped,' Elodie reviews seven years of observed secrets: affairs, forged signatures, a judge who never sleeps. She notices Corin studying the hotel's antique guest registry each night, tracing names with one finger. When she asks, he says only, 'It's a ledger.' Emotional beat: the thrill of a puzzle meeting the guilt of betraying confidences.

chapters.title: Registry of Debts
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Elodie copies pages of the old registry and finds a cipher: room numbers map to dates, marginal ticks to payments. Cross-referencing town archives, she matches entries to unsolved misdeeds spanning sixty years — the ledger is Ashcombe's shadow economy of favors and cover-ups. One entry, dated three weeks out, reads like a contract. Emotional beat: vertigo as the hotel becomes a confession booth.

chapters.title: What Father Filed
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Among the ledger's early keepers, Elodie finds her father's handwriting — he was the hotel's concierge before her, and its archivist. His final entry, the year he died, is circled and annotated: 'the last debt.' Grief and betrayal war as she realizes her inheritance was complicity. Emotional beat: mourning a man she thought she knew.

chapters.title: Thirty Days, Minus Nine
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Elodie and Corin. Corin's interlude reveals he came to Ashcombe to settle his brother's death, ruled accidental years ago — an entry in the ledger. Elodie, unaware, narrows the pending 'contract' to three possible victims, all town notables. They circle each other at the front desk, each testing what the other knows. Emotional beat: two liars negotiating in plain sight.

chapters.title: The Keepers' Dinner
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Invited to cater a private dinner of Ashcombe's founding families, Elodie serves wine and watches four elders react when Corin's name surfaces. Their courtesy is a blade; one, matriarch Vivienne Ashe, quietly warns Elodie: 'Ledgers balance. That's their mercy.' Elodie understands the murder date is a settlement — and she's holding the only copy of the accounts. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Room 12, Vacant
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Deciphering the pending entry fully, Elodie discovers the victim: Corin. The 'murder that hasn't happened yet' is his scheduled execution for reopening old debts. Racing to warn him, she finds Room 12 stripped clean and a note in her father's hand hidden beneath the desk blotter — instructions meant for whoever inherited the ledger. Emotional beat: panic transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: POV: Corin. Corin, captured by the keepers' fixer, learns the town's sheriff is a ledger signatory; there will be no arrest, no trial. He escapes because Elodie, using her encyclopedic knowledge of staff routines and guest patterns, engineers his release from the hotel's service corridors. Together they decide the law can't touch this — but the ledger's own code can. Emotional beat: alliance forged in adrenaline.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. On the murder-eve, during the town's founders' gala in the Verlaine ballroom, Elodie stands at the microphone and reads the ledger aloud — every debt, every signature, including her father's. The room detonates; Vivienne orders her silenced, but too many townspeople hear their own names read back to them. The keepers' power dissolves in collective exposure. Emotional beat: terror becoming terrible, necessary catharsis.

chapters.title: Balanced Books
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. In the aftermath, confessions cascade, prosecutions begin, and Corin — spared — leaves without goodbye, leaving the advance unspent on the front desk. Elodie closes the old registry forever and starts a new book: honest records, kept openly. Her father's last annotation, finally understood, reads 'tell the truth and be free of it.' Emotional beat: grief settled, belonging redefined on her own terms.
